title: Gumroad vs Buy Me a Coffee: Where to Start Selling Digital Products?
summary: Comparing Buy Me a Coffee vs Gumroad for creators — fees, tipping, memberships, and which platform actually fits how you sell.
body_markdown:
For creators comparing platforms to sell digital products, Gumroad and Buy Me a Coffee are close competitors. Both offer simple, intuitive digital storefronts at minimal cost, and are built on a ‘pay as you grow’ model. Though similar from the outside, there’s some fine print that can help you figure out which one fits your specific needs, way of working, and, more importantly, how you wish to grow as a creator.


If you’re at this crossroads, read on. We’ll cover some important considerations that you shouldn’t miss, so you can keep creating, growing, and earning smoothly.


---


### When can your earnings reach you


Let’s start here. Because both Gumroad and Buy Me a Coffee let you earn, no doubt. The difference is when you can actually access that money. Some creators may be perfectly fine waiting until their earnings compound to a bigger sum, while for others it just isn’t practical. This is one of the differences between Gumroad and Buy Me a Coffee.


On Gumroad, you’ll need to **earn a minimum of $100** before you can request a payout, unless you qualify for an instant payout. So, depending on your account and how much you’re earning, you may need to wait until your balance reaches that threshold. For example, you might have made $20 or $40 from your products. You still have a long way ahead of you till you can access any of it. The money doesn’t disappear. It simply stays in your Gumroad balance until you reach the required amount.


Whether this matters to you really depends on how you earn and what you need that money for. If you’re happy letting your earnings build up before withdrawing them, the threshold may not make much of a difference. The wait can feel stressful for creators who rely on smaller amounts.


With Buy Me a Coffee, the payout threshold is


**$10** ,


if you have a Stripe Express account, so even smaller balances can become available for withdrawal sooner. Some users also get their earnings directly to their Stripe account, through Stripe Standard connect. That can be useful if you’re starting out.


So this one really depends on your needs. If you can afford to wait for your earnings to build up to a bigger sum, this aspect won’t matter much. If you’d rather have access to smaller amounts as you earn them, the lower threshold is worth considering.


---


### How much do you keep from each sale?


This is another point of comparison where Gumroad and Buy Me a Coffee vary. Both are free to use, but take a cut from each transaction. It comes down to the percentages and what’s part of the package.


Gumroad charges a **10% flat fee** on sales made through your profile. There’s also Gumroad Discover, where eligible products can be surfaced to people who may not already know you. This bumps up the cut to **30%** . That can be useful if you’re looking for another way for people to find your products, especially if you don’t already have a large audience bringing traffic to your page. At the same time, the higher fee means you’ll want to think about whether the additional exposure is worth it for your particular setup. Being listed there also doesn’t mean every product will necessarily find its way to the right audience.


Buy Me a Coffee, on the other hand, takes a **5% fee** per transaction, and you get access to everything that the platform has to offer.


The gap may seem narrow for now, but it gets more and more visible as you scale. If you make $100 in sales, a 10% platform fee is $10. At 5%, it’s $5. At $500 in sales, that difference becomes $25. At $1,000, it’s $50. And so it goes.


---


### Stay in touch even after the sale


Making a sale matters, that’s the main goal of anyone setting up a shop. But once that transaction ends, how do you keep the door open? The world moves fast, and choices are many. People need hooks, reminders, something that keeps your products at the top of their mind. Sometimes even just your story might be enough to have them come back to your store. This is where having more than just a product page can be useful.


With Gumroad, your storefront is primarily built around the products and other paid offerings you have. You can still build an audience around your work and bring people back through the channels you already use, but that often means taking that relationship beyond the storefront itself.


Buy Me a Coffee gives you more ways to keep your page active between sales. You can share updates, posts, behind-the-scenes efforts, and more about why you do what you do. Basically, it can be a page people return to even when they aren’t buying anything.


That may matter more to some creators than others. If most of your audience already follows you on Instagram, YouTube, Substack, or somewhere else, you may not need your storefront to do much more than sell. But if you want the page itself to be part of your relationship with your audience, it’s another difference to consider.


---


### Keep earning even when there’s nothing to sell


With Gumroad, your earning is mostly tied to having something for people to buy. Which makes sense, that’s what the platform is built for. But what if you don’t have something to sell all the time? Or you simply need a break from creating something new. You can still receive support in other ways.


Buy Me a Coffee lets people do exactly that. Maybe you can take a little breather from your shop, and post what you have to share. And people can still support you through that. There’s provision to send one-time tips, or join a membership plan. You could even mix it up and offer a shop product within your membership plan.


---


### Where does that leave you


The differences might seem minor now but it’s important to keep a note of them. The platform you choose holds your time, effort, and eventually money. Both[Buy Me a Coffee](https://buymeacoffee.com/) and[Gumroad](https://gumroad.com/) do give you a great place to sell your digital products, and what’s different are the nuances. These are just some considerations you can keep at the back of your mind when you choose, so your life as a creator is easier.
